classification: Primary upstream source review; not installed or linked as a firmware dependency
hardware_decision: Not directly usable on admitted ESP32-D0WD-V3 boards. Upstream explicitly excludes classic ESP32 because it lacks FTM. Pinned SDK ESP_WIFI_FTM_ENABLE depends on SOC_WIFI_FTM_SUPPORT, which is absent for original ESP32.
useful_concepts: Separate hardware timestamp acquisition, clock phase/frequency estimation and hardware output-timer control.
Use a sliding clock-relationship fit with reference-centered arithmetic and independent forward/inverse mapping.
Correct both phase and rate; fractional timer-period dithering can approximate a desired mean period.
Extend the32-bit MAC clock and explicitly monitor discontinuities/wrap.
review_cautions: Their CRM consumes hardware FTM timestamp exchanges. Feeding callback or enqueue timestamps into it is not equivalent.
The inspected CRM sets validity from R-squared and contains a TODO for slope magnitude validation. Our model needs slope/residual/age/epoch gates; a high R-squared alone is insufficient.
The inspected timer path aborts for invalid periods and has a recovery TODO; avoid importing that behavior into continuous audio.
The inspected clock helper serializes reads with a mutex. It is not a radio-ISR drop-in.
README timer granularity and jitter claims concern their FTM-enabled hardware/setup; they do not prove PCM5102A/I2S synchronization or our RF/audio performance.
licensing: Upstream GPL-3.0. No source copied into our independently authored protocol modules.
continued_work: Use native original-ESP32 MAC RX timestamps/beacon-reference research as the measurement input, preserve the independently authored wrap-safe/sample-timeline foundation, and continue custom Wi-Fi/BTstack bring-up.
